answer.what_it_does: Booking.com’s AI Trip Planner is a conversational travel-planning feature that helps travelers ask general and specific trip questions, explore destinations and accommodations, and build itineraries. Booking later expanded it with AI-powered features and agentic experiences aimed at easier search, smarter decisions, and in-trip assistance.

ai_agents.what_it_does: Answers travelers’ property-related questions in a conversational flow.
actions: Matches property mentions to the correct Booking.com property ID
Fetches relevant information from internal systems
Calculates distances and travel times to landmarks and transportation hubs

ai_agents.name: AI Trip Planner
ai_agents.what_it_does: Helps travelers plan trips by answering travel questions, suggesting destinations and accommodations, and generating itineraries.
actions: Processes natural-language travel prompts
Searches destination and accommodation options
Generates itineraries for cities, countries, or regions
Uses real-time availability and pricing data from Booking.com

actions: Supports destination discovery
Supports accommodation comparison
Supports itinerary building
Supports answering questions during the trip-planning and in-trip stages

incidents_or_risks.what: Public sources describe Booking.com’s shift from a standalone AI Trip Planner toward embedded and agentic AI features, but no public incident specific to the AI Trip Planner was identified in the search results.

Industry coverage notes the strategic risk that AI agents could bypass online travel intermediaries, although Booking argues its inventory, payments, and supplier relationships make it a strong partner for those systems.

facts.claim: Booking.com launched the AI Trip Planner in June 2023.
Travelers can use the AI Trip Planner to ask both general and specific travel-related questions.
Booking.com said the AI Trip Planner can help create itineraries for a city, country, or region.
Booking.com’s AI Trip Planner can incorporate real-time availability and pricing data from Booking.com’s database.
Booking.com has described AgentHub as an internal platform for building modular, production-grade AI agents and workflows.
One of the first agents built on AgentHub was the AI Trip Planner Q&A.
Booking.com has publicly said its AI features are evolving into an embedded AI-powered companion across the booking journey.

answer.what_it_does: Booking.com’s AI Trip Planner lets travelers describe trip ideas in natural language and receive conversational suggestions such as destination and accommodation options, itinerary concepts, and travel inspiration. It’s integrated into Booking.com’s booking flow, surfacing visual lists with deep-links to property details and enabling users to complete reservations from within the app interface.

ai_agents.name: AI Trip Planner (conversational trip planning agent)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Guides trip discovery and planning via chat by interpreting traveler intent and generating destination/accommodation recommendations and itinerary ideas, then linking back to relevant Booking.com properties and pricing/availability.
actions: Collects user intent through chat prompts describing travel preferences and constraints
Generates destination and accommodation recommendations and itinerary suggestions based on user inputs
Displays a visual list of destinations/properties including Booking.com pricing and deep-links to details
Enables users to reserve by connecting chat results to the accommodation booking experience in the Booking.com app

ai_agents.name: AI Trip Support / agentic customer-service support (embedded AI tools around the trip journey)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Provides automated, context-aware customer service responses for common trip questions and can hand off to human representatives for more complex issues, using booking/property context pulled to answer traveler questions.
actions: Acts as a first point of contact for travelers with 24/7 guidance on customer service topics
Gathers relevant information from the property context to answer questions (e.g., parking availability) to support independent reservation changes
Facilitates handover to an informed customer service representative for complex questions
Connects to other support flows when needed

what_the_agent_can_reach: Booking.com customer-facing app interface (chat experience and recommendation UI)

Accommodation booking/reservation functionality via deep-links/integration in the app

use_cases.name: Automated property/trip Q&A and faster support resolution during the booking journey
use_cases.who_uses_it: Travelers needing trip-related information and support (especially for questions that can be answered using property and booking context).
what_the_agent_can_reach: Property-related information used to answer traveler questions (e.g., parking availability)
Reservation/change flows that depend on accurate trip information
Booking.com customer service representative handover workflow (human support escalation)

incidents_or_risks.what: Risk of incomplete or inaccurate information being published from recommender systems (control recommendation to improve completeness/accuracy).

facts.claim: Booking.com’s AI Trip Planner is built on Booking.com’s existing ML models that recommend destination and accommodation options, and it is partially powered by LLM technology from OpenAI’s ChatGPT API.

The AI Trip Planner can handle general travel questions as well as more specific queries across multiple stages of trip planning, including scoping destinations/accommodations and creating itineraries for a city/country/region.
Booking.com states the AI Trip Planner integrates into the accommodation booking experience in the Booking.com app, allowing users to complete reservations from the AI planner’s recommendations.

OpenAI reports that Booking.com integrated its data systems with OpenAI LLMs to deliver intent-driven travel experiences and that the AI Trip Planner pulls real-time availability and pricing data from Booking.com.

answer.what_it_does: The Booking.com AI Trip Planner is a generative AI-powered tool that allows travelers to plan trips through natural language conversations, providing personalized recommendations for destinations, accommodations, and activities. It integrates real-time inventory, pricing, and property data to help users scope out travel options, build detailed itineraries, and transition directly into the booking process.

incidents_or_risks.what: General risks associated with AI travel planning include inaccurate information, 'hallucinations' (generating false details), outdated pricing, and privacy concerns regarding input data.
High consumer concern regarding data privacy, security, and the potential for AI to act without explicit user confirmation on financial transactions.

facts.claim: Booking.com developed 'AgentHub', an internal platform that allows teams to build and deploy modular AI agents for various travel services.
The AI Trip Planner was built by combining Booking.com's existing machine learning infrastructure with the OpenAI ChatGPT API.

answer.what_it_does: Booking.com's AI Trip Planner is a conversational feature in its app that helps travelers explore destinations, draft itineraries and move from chat to an accommodation booking, built on OpenAI large language models and the company's existing recommendation models. The company is also building an in-house agent platform, AgentHub, that powers trip-planning, search, partner-messaging and trip-management agents across the booking funnel.

ai_agents.name: AI Trip Planner (conversational trip planning agent)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Answers open-ended travel questions in chat, suggests destinations and stays, and builds itineraries, then links travelers to bookable properties in the app.
actions: Answers general travel questions and destination or accommodation queries in a chat interface
Produces visual lists of destinations and properties with Booking.com pricing and deep links
Lets users complete an accommodation reservation in the app from the chat
Uses OpenAI LLM capabilities via API on top of Booking.com's existing machine learning recommendation models
Pulls real-time availability and pricing data, per OpenAI's case study

ai_agents.name: AI Trip Planner Q&A agent (built on AgentHub)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Answers traveler questions about specific properties in a conversational way, and was one of the first agents built on AgentHub.
actions: Matches property mentions in a user's message to the correct Booking.com property ID
Fetches property information from internal Booking.com systems
Calculates distances and travel times for the traveler
Operates within the AgentHub platform's guardrails

ai_agents.name: Smart Messenger (partner-facing messaging agent)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Helps accommodation partners reply to guest messages by suggesting and sending responses, and learns from past interactions and feedback.
actions: Gathers partner, property and reservation information to decide what to suggest or do
Generates responses to guest messages on behalf of partners in the Extranet
Works with partner-defined Auto-Reply topics for common and unique guest questions
Learns from past interactions and user feedback

ai_agents.name: AI Voice Support and trip-management assistant
ai_agents.what_it_does: Provides voice-powered trip management for travelers with existing reservations and can hand off to a human agent when needed.
actions: Reads the traveler's booking details to answer trip-management questions, such as cancellation requests
Escalates to a human customer-support agent and passes along the case context
Currently runs on English and German phone lines, with Italian and Spanish in testing

ai_agents.name: AI Rental Helper (car rental assistant)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Answers common customer questions about a car rental booking and explains its lengthy terms.
actions: Answers questions about the customer's car rental booking and terms and conditions

incidents_or_risks.what: Booking.com's 2025 annual report warned that AI agents may evolve into full-service booking platforms, adding competitive pressure and disintermediating online travel companies (as quoted by a third-party analysis).
Booking.com's CFO said traffic from large language models is significantly below 1% of room nights, paid and unpaid combined, so AI-agent exposure is currently small.

Booking.com's chief business officer said the company built AI orchestration tools it now regrets, because frontier model makers later shipped the same capabilities, and that for Booking.com the main failure mode would be irrelevant content or wrong prices.
Booking.com research found 89% of people want to use AI to research travel but only 6% trust it to make travel decisions, which the company cites as a trust barrier to agentic booking.
Booking.com's Chief Business Officer said travel is among the last categories expected to move to agentic commerce, and that LLMs are used for research but not yet for booking.

facts.claim: The AI Trip Planner was announced in June 2023 as a beta for selected US Genius members in the Booking.com app and was built partly on OpenAI's ChatGPT API.
By late 2024 the AI Trip Planner had expanded via the mobile app to the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand and Singapore.
Booking.com's AI Trip Planner was launched within about 10 weeks of starting with OpenAI's API and a hackathon, according to OpenAI's customer story.
Booking.com reported that its Property Q&A feature lowered support volumes through more accurate in-app answers, and that Smart Filters reduced search time.
AgentHub is Booking.com's internal platform for building LLM-driven travel agents; teams can build and deploy agents in hours using configuration and reusable components.
AgentHub includes guardrails such as prompt-injection detection, PII filtering and jailbreak prevention.
Booking.com plans to add multi-agent collaboration, multimodal inputs, long-term memory and personalization to AgentHub, which it describes as still evolving.
Booking.com reports its hybrid strategy, including selective work with OpenAI, has roughly doubled accuracy across key retrieval, ranking and customer-interaction tasks.
Booking.com says Smart Messenger's early experiments produced a 73% increase in partner satisfaction compared with previous messaging tools.
